## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Nigrodhakappa Sutta* (also designated as the *Vaṅgīsa Sutta* or *Kappa Sutta* in traditional *uddāna* verses and commentaries) is the twelfth discourse of the *Cūḷavagga* in the *Suttanipāta* [Norman 1997-2001; Anderson & Smith 1913; Saddhatissa 2013]. The text is set at the Aggāḷava Shrine near Āḷavī shortly after the death of the Venerable Nigrodhakappa, who served as the preceptor (*upajjhāya*) of the Venerable Vaṅgīsa [Hazra 1994; Saddhatissa 2013; Buswell & Lopez 2014]. Vaṅgīsa—celebrated as the foremost poet among the disciples of the Buddha—inquires while in seclusion whether his recently deceased mentor had attained full Nibbāna (*parinibbuto*) or if any residue of existence remained [Hazra 1994; Saddhatissa 2013; Buswell & Lopez 2014]. Approaching the Buddha in the evening, Vaṅgīsa poses his questions in elegant verse [Saddhatissa 2013; Anderson & Smith 1913]. The Buddha confirms that Nigrodhakappa cut off all craving for name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*) and severed the deceptive snare of death (*maccuno jālaṁ*), attaining complete parinibbāna, whereupon Vaṅgīsa extols the Master in further verses of praise [Hazra 1994; Ñāṇananda, Magic of the mind; Saddhatissa 2013; Buswell & Lopez 2014].

 DharmaNexus corroborates this alignment, recording an extensive Pali-internal match of 3,649 characters where verses §1.9–17.4 correspond at 0.98 similarity to Thag §55.1–70.4 [DharmaNexus]. Textual reuse is also registered across the commentaries (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* and *Suttanipāta-aṭṭhakathā*), the *Vaṅgīsa Saṁyutta* (SN 8), and various Vinaya Khandhaka treatises [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus further detects low-scoring automated cross-language alignments with Tibetan canonical texts, including the Tibetan translation of the *Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra* (D0119-2) and the *Mahāmayūrīvidyārājñī* (D0559) [DharmaNexus].
